messages:
neil: Opening a 60m change window to run a canary publish for py/ts SDKs. Goal: test publish flow + consumer compatibility. Plan: npm tag `canary-3612345678`, push to pypi-staging, route 8% internal. @sam will publish, @maria_s update notes.

sam: Artifacts built. Will run: `npm publish --tag canary-3612345678` and `twine upload --repository-url https://test.pypi.org/legacy/ dist/*`.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: starting publish job for canary-3612345678 -> internal npm + pypi-staging. CI: https://ci.redwood.example/3612345678/logs

maria_s: Drafted release-note stub: "internal canary: no GA changes. Callout: legacy sync client deprecation reminder + migration link." Draft: https://docs.redwood.example/drafts/canary-3612345678

jen: Feature flag set to 8% (`sdk_canary_percent`). Monitoring hooks: p50/p99 latency, error-rate, memory. Abort if p99 > +10% or errors >1% absolute.

ops-bot: ops-bot: Observability alert: p99 latency spike detected in eu-west-1 for canary cohort (+12%).

neil: Pausing rollout. @sam remove dist-tag and stop routing. Can you pin infra to stable 1.3.2 if needed?

sam: Running rollback: `npm dist-tag rm @redwood/sdk canary-3612345678`. Removing staging artifact. Flipping feature flag back to 0%.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rollback complete. Traffic reverted to stable release. Rollback CI: https://ci.redwood.example/3612345678/rollback status: success.

maria_s: Updating release notes: "Canary paused due to regional perf regression; stable release unchanged. Investigating bundler change. Follow-up scheduled." I'll also add the pinback PR link when available.

sam: Opened pinback PR to pin internal consumers to 1.3.2: https://github.com/redwood/internal-configs/pull/450

neil: Action items: 1) revert bundler/minify tweak on canary branch, 2) add perf test for eu-west-1 workload, 3) re-run canary next Tue 14:00 UTC after fixes. Assigning owners in ticket. Thanks all.
